details.detail: Overall massing and layout. The 1.30 m shell, 2.20 m pitch, aisle wardrobe, window console, lowered centre divider, ottoman and table all still match the real photos. The narrow centre suite is known and not scored.

Centre fin between the D and G screens: REGRESSED. The w4 solid half-wedges now merge into ONE THICK DARK POST about 0.20 m wide at its aft face, full cap height (q02 x 415-490 y 130-310; s3 crop). It reads as a wooden pillar. Real photos settle the w4 question: f32 (2D/2G), f33 (1D/1G) and tlfl_14 (divider raised) all show ONE THIN (about 0.02 m) wood panel standing ON THE CENTRELINE, in the divider plane. It is about 0.30-0.35 deep from the screen wall and runs from table level (about 0.64) to just above the screen top (about 1.23). A light greige edge strip about 0.02-0.025 wide runs along its top and aft edges. In tlfl_14 it is visibly the forward extension of the raised divider, not angled.

Window-suite screen wall: pier, mirror, lamp and wing. The layout is right: a wood wing on the window side, and on the aisle side an angled pier with the pill mirror and the black eyeball lamp at its upper outer corner. f_17313 confirms a steeply angled pier. From the seat (q03), the pier projects 52 px against the 315 px screen, about 0.16 m. f11 shows about 0.30 m (190 px against 600 px), though from further forward. The mirror is far too bright and blue: q03 116/132/157 against the neighbouring pier wood 45/35/32 (3.2x), where f11 has mirror 91/113/126 against pier wood 96/100/106 (1.0x, teal-grey reflecting the wood). The console-end taupe tab (0.12 x 0.02 x 0.14 fCap at y 0.70) reads as a floating light chip in q03 (x 345-380 y 320-335) and q05. In f11 the console's forward end is a dark wood-topped block flush with the table (x 825-945).

Forward aisle hood. From the aisle (q02 2G) it is a good match for f32/f33: a thick rounded arm over the leaf, overhanging the aisle. From inside (q03 x 700-840 y 85-135) it is still a rolled bolster whose inboard edge hangs over the pier top; in f11 the inside corner is a flat thin band.

Aisle leaves (exterior). Rib count is 15 per leaf by design (real about 23). The luminance ratio of the fluted field to the cap is RIGHT: s6 90/190 = 0.47 against f60 82/175 = 0.47. But the dark-groove fraction is 0.62 in s6 against 0.30 in f60: the real leaf is broad flat slats with narrow dark slits, and ours reads as thin rods on a dark ground. The frame/field ratio is 1.63 (s6 147 against 90) against 1.17 real (f60 96 against 82), so the frame reads as a light picture frame. The exposed dark-wood panel aft of the aft leaf in open state (0.38 wide) is not clearly seen in open-door photos f7/f58, where the parked aft leaf covers most of the wardrobe run under the cap.

Seat, niche, reading spots and headrest flap. The niche with two eyeball lamps in the header corners matches f9/f57. Flap/back luminance is 1.16x against f9 1.12x, neutral grey: good. The back has two horizontal seams (f9 shows channel quilting, close enough). The studio seat pan renders beige 189/179/167 from the top light (lighting only).

Armrest (aisle side). The model has a solid 0.10 taupe box with a taupe top. In f9 and f57 the armrest is a slim rounded taupe PAD (about 0.08 wide x 0.05 thick, rounded front end) on a dark-WOOD body/face, which reads as part of the wood wardrobe wall.
Seat-mode pillow: correct lavender (model 128/117/185 against f9 161/148/227, lighting-limited), rectangular and plump. The diamond jacquard is missing.

Window console, keypad, handset and tray. The keypad, handset and dock are good. The tray is a flat tapered wood inlay in a black rim. In tlfl_14, f5 and f58 it is a long sculpted recessed tray: a dark interior whose taupe rim sweeps up at the forward end.

Ottoman, table and aisle box. The ottoman shape and tone are good: q03 113/105/96 against f11 123/107/100. The table is slightly dark (0.73x the ottoman, real 0.94x). The aisle box has no lid latch; f11 has a dark recessed latch at the top inboard edge.

Bed mode. The pillows are right (white propped, lavender low in front, as in f57). The duvet is on the window half as in f57, but pad and duvet are the same white (230 against 232), so q04 reads as one white slab. The white pad is also full seat width. In f57 the pad is narrower, so a strip of dark tweed about 0.10-0.12 wide shows along the aisle side, and the black seatbelt lies across the pad. f58/f59 show the duvet with a turned-down diagonal corner. The sun stripes are lighting and out of scope.

Seat plaque (09_seats.js, integrator). A dark tile with light text lying on the forward end of the wardrobe cap is the RIGHT concept (f60 '2K': tile 138/124/98 against cap 179/166/133, 0.77x; f9: blue-lit characters). It is still a little oversized, about 0.068 x 0.038 against a real size of about 0.045 x 0.025.

issues.issue: The centre fin is a thick dark wooden post; the real part is ONE thin panel on the centreline
issues.evidence: q02_suiteAisle.png x 415-490 y 130-310 and s3_suiteC.png: a square pillar about 0.20 m wide at its aft face, full cap height, with a split top. omaat_f32 (2D/2G crop 400-640 x 320-700): one thin wood board with a light greige top edge and aft edge strip, in the divider plane. omaat_f33 (1D/1G): the same thin board. tlfl_14: with the divider raised, the board is coplanar with the divider and is its forward extension to the screen wall; in that photo it is about 0.35 deep (75 px against 345 px of divider). Real wood tone f32 58/48/39 against model 47/36/33, which is fine.
issues.fix: 09d_suite.js line 61-62 (center branch): delete the gExtrude wedge. Each half (mirrored by the neighbour) builds: B.add(gRBox(0.012, 0.58, 0.34, 0.003, 1), M4.trs(-hx + 0.006, 0.64 + 0.29, -L + 0.12 + 0.17), SEATMAT.fWood); plus a greige edge: B.add(gRBox(0.013, 0.022, 0.35, 0.004, 1), M4.trs(-hx + 0.0065, 1.231, -L + 0.295), SEATMAT.fCap) (top) and B.add(gRBox(0.013, 0.60, 0.022, 0.004, 1), M4.trs(-hx + 0.0065, 0.93, -L + 0.455), SEATMAT.fCap) (aft edge). Total thickness is 0.024 with the mirror. It sits in the 0.03 gap between the divider plane and the bezel (the centre wing is 0), so it clears the screen. Keep the grain horizontal, as now.

issues.issue: Bed mode reads as one white slab: no tweed margin, no seatbelt, no turned-down duvet corner
issues.evidence: q04 bed 232/230/226 against duvet about 230: no separation. omaat_f57: the white pad is narrower than the bed surface, leaving about 0.10-0.12 of dark tweed along the aisle side; the duvet is folded on the window half; the black belt with a silver buckle lies across the pad. omaat_f58/f59 and f_17304: the duvet has a diagonal turned-down corner at the head end.
issues.fix: Line 218: make the pad cushionSecs(SW - 0.12, 1.96, ...) at M4.trs(seatX - 0.07, 0.44, -1.08), and add a tweed bed base under it: B.add(gRBox(SW, 0.05, 1.96, 0.02, 1), M4.trs(seatX - 0.01, 0.405, -1.08), SEATMAT.fFabric). Belt: two gBox(0.035, 0.004, 0.30) SEATMAT.black straps on the aisle half at y 0.505, rotated ±25 deg about y around (seatX + 0.12, -0.75), plus a SEATMAT.buckle 0.05 x 0.012 x 0.035 at their meeting point. Duvet corner: gExtrude([[0,0],[0.32,0],[0,0.40]], 0.018) in '#e6e2da' at the duvet's aft-aisle corner (x = seatX - SW*0.17 + SW*0.31, z = -0.40, y 0.585), lying flat (rx -π/2) and reading as the folded-back flap.

issues.issue: The pier mirror is a bright light-blue pill, about 3x the neighbouring wood, where the real mirror has about the same luminance as the wood
issues.evidence: q03 mirror 116/132/157 against pier wood 45/35/32. omaat_f11 mirror 91/113/126 (teal-grey, reflecting the wood) against pier wood 96/100/106.
issues.fix: Line 13: fMirror c '#8593a8' -> '#4d5d6a', r 0.12, m 0.35. It then reads as a dark reflective slab like f11/f5 (f5 x 820-895: a dark pill barely lighter than the wood). Pier wood near-black in the cabin is lighting (out of scope).

issues.issue: The door leaves read as thin rods on a dark ground inside a light picture frame; the real leaves are broad slats with narrow slits in a same-tone frame
issues.evidence: Dark-groove fraction: s6 0.62 against omaat_f60 0.30. Frame/field luminance: s6 147/90 = 1.63 against f60 96/82 = 1.17. The field/cap ratio already matches (0.47 against 0.47).
issues.fix: Line 186: rib gCyl radius 0.0075 -> 0.0095 (rib 0.019 of the 0.026 pitch, about 27 % groove) and flatten it with a 0.6 scale in x (M4.trs(...) then scale(0.6,1,1), or build it as gRBox(0.008, H-0.34, 0.019, 0.004, 1)) so the crest is a broad flat. Line 11: fDoorFrame c '#655d53' -> '#57524a', so the frame sits at about 1.15x the fluted field. Keep 15 ribs per leaf (the deliberate moiré trade-off).

issues.issue: The armrest is a solid taupe box; the real one is a slim rounded taupe pad on a dark-wood body
issues.evidence: omaat_f57 crop 700-1150 x 380-900: a rounded taupe pad about 0.08 wide and 0.05 thick with a rounded forward end, on a wood face with vertical grain. omaat_f9 x 800-850: wood below the pad.
issues.fix: Line 209: armrest body material SEATMAT.fConsole -> SEATMAT.fWood (or add a 0.004 fWood skin on its -x face, gRBox(0.004, 0.56, 0.60) at local (ax - 0.051, 0.30, -0.40)). Line 210: replace the flat fShell top with B.add(gRBox(0.085, 0.05, 0.66, 0.024, 3), M4.mul(S, M4.trs(ax, 0.645, -0.41)), SEATMAT.fCap), a rounded pad that overhangs 0.02 forward. Move the literature-pocket fInner quad on line 211 so it stays on the wood face.

issues.evidence: q03 x 345-380 y 320-335 and q05 x 350-375: a light rectangle. omaat_f11 x 825-945 y 400-460: a dark striped wood top level with the stowed table, over a taupe body.
issues.fix: Line 57: replace the 0.12 x 0.02 x 0.14 fCap tab at y 0.70 with B.add(gRBox(shelfW, 0.035, 0.24, 0.008, 1), M4.trs(xo + shelfW / 2, 0.6425, -L + 0.25), SEATMAT.fShelf) and a taupe body B.add(gRBox(shelfW, 0.10, 0.24, 0.01, 1), M4.trs(xo + shelfW / 2, 0.575, -L + 0.25), SEATMAT.fConsole), so the table line continues to the wing.

issues.fix: After line 86: B.add(gRBox(0.06, 0.012, 0.025, 0.004, 1), M4.trs(bX0 + 0.05, 0.615, -L + 0.47), SEATMAT.black). Pillow: apply the shared diamond layer if one exists. Plaque: 09_seats.js (integrator), scale the tile to about 0.045 x 0.025.

issues.evidence: Sun stripes wash the bed (q04) and the ottoman (q03). The pier and wing wood render near-black (q03 45/35/32 against f11 96/100/106). Cabin-lit real photos (f33/f60) are warmer and more olive: cap 175/164/132 against q02 190/184/172.

questions: The fin between centre screens: the photos (omaat_f32, f33, tlfl_14) show one thin panel in the divider plane. Can you confirm, so the V/wedge approach is dropped for good?

Aisle leaves when OPEN: in omaat_f7/f58 the parked aft leaf seems to cover most of the wardrobe run under the cap (leaving little dark wood exposed aft), while the model parks it at z -0.96..-0.46 and shows 0.38 m of wood aft of it.
